name: Ceftriaxone
summary: Once-daily third-generation cephalosporin with broad Gram-negative coverage and excellent CSF penetration; a hospital workhorse.
mechanism: Beta-lactam inhibition of penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs) blocks cell-wall synthesis; enhanced activity against Gram-negative organisms vs earlier generations.
pharmacodynamics: Time-dependent killing; long half-life permits once-daily dosing.

dosing.adult: 1-2 g IV/IM once daily (meningitis: 2 g every 12 hours)

safety.lactation: Compatible — minimal excretion in breast milk
contraindications: Concurrent IV calcium in neonates (precipitation risk)
monitoring: Signs of biliary sludging on prolonged therapy
CBC with prolonged use (rare hemolytic anemia)

clinicalPearls: Excellent CSF penetration — standard empiric meningitis therapy (with vancomycin)
good: Once-daily broad-spectrum IV agent with CNS and gonococcal coverage.
bad: No MRSA or Listeria activity (add vancomycin/ampicillin when relevant); avoid in jaundiced neonates.
